n: After being driven from Nauvoo in 1846, the Saints wintered at Winter Quarters (near today’s Omaha, Nebraska). On January 14, 1847, Brigham Young received this revelation for the “Camp of Israel”—a deliberate echo of ancient Israel in the wilderness.
Everyone—members and those traveling with them—should be organized into companies and covenant to keep God’s commandments.
Companies have captains over hundreds, fifties, and tens, each led by a president and two counselors under the Twelve—a pattern from Moses.

f.w: captains of hundreds, captains of fifties, and captains of tens

n: Their covenant: to walk in all the Lord’s ordinances. Many had just received temple endowments in Nauvoo before leaving.

f.w: walk in all the ordinances of the Lord

n: Each company should gather all the wagons, animals, food, and clothing it can.

f.g: Animals (usually oxen) harnessed to pull wagons.

n: Once organized, they should work hard to prepare for those staying behind.

f.g: Get to work with all their strength.

n: Each company decides who can go in the spring and selects skilled pioneers to go ahead with seeds and tools to plant crops.

f.g: An advance company; Brigham Young led the first group of 148 in April 1847.

n: Each company must share fairly in caring for the poor, widows, orphans, and families of men in the Mormon Battalion, so the cries of the needy do not rise against them.

f.w: the families of those who have gone into the army
f.g: About 500 men had enlisted in the Mormon Battalion in 1846 for the Mexican–American War.

f.w: the cries of the widow and the fatherless

n: Companies should build homes and plant fields for those who must remain.

f.w: those who are to remain behind
f.g: Way stations such as Garden Grove and Mount Pisgah in Iowa served later emigrants.

n: Everyone should use their influence and property to move the people to the place where the Lord will set up a stake of Zion.

f.g: This proved to be the Salt Lake Valley, reached July 1847.

n: If done with a pure heart, they will be blessed in flocks, herds, fields, homes, and families.
Ezra T. Benson and Erastus Snow are to organize a company.

f.g: Ordained an apostle in 1846; great-grandfather of President Ezra Taft Benson.

n: Orson Pratt and Wilford Woodruff organize another.

f.g: An apostle and scientist; he and Erastus Snow were the first of the pioneers to enter the Salt Lake Valley.

n: Amasa Lyman and George A. Smith organize another.

f.g: Cousin of Joseph Smith, later a counselor to Brigham Young.

n: They should appoint presidents and captains at each level.
These leaders should teach the Lord’s will so the Saints are ready to go to a land of peace.

f.g: After years of persecution, the Saints longed for a place to live undisturbed.

n: Go forward without fear; enemies cannot stop God’s work.

f.w: they shall not have power to stop my work

n: Zion will be redeemed in the Lord’s own time.
Anyone who seeks self-promotion and ignores the Lord’s counsel will lose power and be exposed. After Joseph’s death, several men tried to lead the Church in their own way.

f.g: Some claimants to leadership after 1844 drew followers away.

n: Keep your promises to one another and don’t covet.

f.w: covet not that which is thy brother's

n: Don’t take the Lord’s name in vain; he is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

f.w: take the name of the Lord in vain

n: The same God who led Israel out of Egypt is stretching out his arm to save his people now—a direct comparison with the Exodus.

f.w: I am he who led the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt

n: Stop quarreling and speaking evil of one another.

f.w: cease to speak evil one of another

n: Stop drunkenness; let your words build each other up.
Return what you borrow; if you can’t, tell your neighbor promptly.

f.w: restore that which thou hast borrowed

n: If you find something your neighbor lost, search until you return it.

f.w: that which thy neighbor has lost

n: Take good care of what you have; it is God’s gift, and you are his steward.
A cheerful command: when happy, praise the Lord with singing, music, dancing, and prayer. Pioneers famously danced around campfires on the trail.
When sorrowful, pray to the Lord so your soul may find joy.
Do not fear enemies; they are in God’s hands.
God’s people must be tested in everything to prepare for Zion’s glory. Those unwilling to accept correction are not ready for the kingdom.
The ignorant can learn wisdom by humbling themselves and praying, so their eyes and ears are opened.

f.w: that his eyes may be opened

n: God’s Spirit enlightens the humble and penitent but condemns the ungodly.
The nation that drove them out has rejected their testimony.

f.w: the nation that has driven you out
f.g: The Saints were expelled from Missouri and Illinois without government protection.

n: Calamity will come on that nation like labor pains unless it repents quickly. Many later saw the Civil War as fulfillment.

f.w: like a woman that is taken in travail

n: They killed the prophets, and innocent blood cries out from the ground—as Abel’s did.
Don’t be surprised; the Saints are not yet pure enough to bear God’s glory. But if faithful to his word—from Adam to Joseph Smith—they will see it.

f.w: ye can not yet bear my glory

n: Joseph laid the foundation faithfully, and the Lord took him home.
Many were troubled by Joseph’s death, but it was necessary that he seal his testimony with his blood, bringing him honor and condemnation on the wicked.

f.w: seal his testimony with his blood

n: God delivered his people, except that he left a witness of his name in the martyred prophet.
Listen, members and elders: you have received the kingdom.
Be diligent in obedience, lest judgment come, faith fail, and enemies prevail. This is the only revelation canonized from Brigham Young.

f.g: A plain closing, as in a letter.
